title: Hall's marriage theorem: a finite family of finite sets has a system of distinct representatives if and only if every sub-family covers at least its own size
statement: Let nb be a family of finite sets of naturals indexed by the naturals, and let s be a finite index set. Then Hall's condition holds on s -- every subset t of s satisfies card t <= card (union over t of nb) -- if and only if there is a function f that sends each index of s to a member of its own set and is injective on s. That is Hall's marriage theorem, in both directions, as a single biconditional. The sufficiency direction is proved by strong induction on card s: an explicit bounded search decides whether some nonempty proper subset of s is critical, the critical branch matches that subset and its complement separately against a family with the critical neighbourhood deleted and glues the two, and the non-critical branch commits one index to a neighbour and recurses on the rest against a family with that one value deleted. There is no choice principle in this kernel, so every witness is computed. This is a kernel term with an empty axiom footprint.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Hall.marriage_iff : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> AxNat.Finset)) -> Iff (AxNat.Hall.HallCondition x0 x1) (Exists.{1} (((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) (fun (x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) => AxNat.Hall.IsMatching x0 x1 x2))))
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.Hall.HallCondition s nb := forall t, (forall i, memB t i = true -> memB s i = true) -> Le (card t) (card (unionOver nb t)); Nat.Hall.IsMatching s nb f := And (forall i, memB s i = true -> memB (nb i) (f i) = true) (forall i j, memB s i = true -> memB s j = true -> Eq Nat (f i) (f j) -> Eq Nat i j). The sufficiency direction alone is Nat.Hall.sufficient : forall s nb, HallCondition s nb -> Exists (fun f => IsMatching s nb f); the necessity direction is Nat.Hall.hallCondition_of_isMatching, proved in ADR-1608. Landed with the assembly: Nat.Hall.criticalB (the Bool-valued decision the subset search consumes), Nat.Hall.criticalB_congr, Nat.Hall.isMatching_of_family_sdiff, Nat.Hall.memB_false_of_family_sdiff, and Nat.Finset.memB_sdiff_congr.

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `hall-assembly`, roadmap item W2-12, sixth and final slice: `nat_prelude/hall_marriage.rs`. ADR-1645, completing ADR-1608, ADR-1614, ADR-1623, ADR-1630 and ADR-1644.
provenance.source: The standard inductive proof, split on whether a nonempty proper subset of the index set is critical.

prior_art.citation: P. Hall, 'On Representatives of Subsets', J. London Math. Soc. 10 (1935) 26-30

prior_art.establishes: the theorem over `Finset` in Lean 4, with classical choice and set extensionality available; that proof selects a critical subset with `Classical.choice` over a decidable-but-unenumerated existential and identifies extensionally equal finsets, where this route must run an explicit bounded search over subsets and carry a stored bound that extensionally equal sets need not share

prior_art.citation: M. Hall Jr., 'Distinct representatives of subsets', Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 54 (1948) 922-926
prior_art.establishes: the infinite-index version; not in scope here -- the statement proved is the finite one, with the index set a `Nat.Finset`

evidence.supports: Hall's condition and the existence of a system of distinct representatives are equivalent
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
nat_prelude::hall_marriage_tests::halls_marriage_theorem_is_admitted_and_axiom_free (Environment::contains and the declaration KIND before axiom_footprint)
evidence.notes: The forward direction is Nat.Hall.sufficient; the backward direction is Nat.Hall.hallCondition_of_isMatching (ADR-1608) under one Exists.rec to name the matching. Both halves and all five supporting declarations are covered by the same footprint sweep, and each footprint assertion is preceded by Environment::contains, because an empty axiom footprint is also what a missing name returns.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Exchanging the critical and non-critical branches of the inductive step -- passing the `anySubset = false` case function where the `= true` case is demanded and vice versa, which is type-correct Rust -- was RUN as mutant 2 of SUITES["hall-marriage-in-kernel"]: killed 44 of a 44-test baseline, by kernel rejection at declaration.

evidence.supports: the admitted statement relates Hall's condition to an EXISTENTIAL over choice functions, in the right direction
evidence.notes: The footprint sweep cannot see a statement drift: an Iff whose two sides were the same proposition, or whose right side quantified a FIXED choice function rather than existentially, would be admitted and axiom-free just as happily. The test reads the rendered type out of the kernel environment and requires Iff, Nat.Hall.HallCondition, Nat.Hall.IsMatching and Exists all to appear; it then reads Nat.Hall.sufficient's type and requires HallCondition to occur BEFORE Exists, so the implication is not the converse.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The ordering assertion is the paired negative: a statement with the existential as hypothesis and Hall's condition as conclusion -- which is necessity, already proved and therefore trivially admissible under this name -- fails it.

evidence.supports: the search predicate computes the decision it claims to, with each conjunct load-bearing at a different instance
evidence.notes: The kernel cannot tell a Definition is wrong: Nat.Hall.criticalB type-checks at Finset -> (Nat -> Finset) -> Finset -> Bool and so does `fun _ _ _ => true`. So it is reduced at closed arguments against hand-computed verdicts, one row per conjunct. The two `ble 1 ...` conjuncts are the two nonemptiness facts the two recursive calls need and they sit on OPPOSITE sides of the split: without `0 < card t` the branch fires at t = empty and recurses on sdiff s empty at the same count; without `0 < card (sdiff s t)` it fires at t = s and recurses on t at the same count. The second test asserts the four counts that make each accepted by the other's test, so the pair is shown not to be one condition written twice.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Collapsing the two positivity conjuncts into one -- replacing `ble 1 (card (sdiff s t))` with a second copy of `ble 1 (card t)` -- was RUN as mutant 3 of SUITES["hall-marriage-in-kernel"]: killed 44 of a 44-test baseline.

evidence.supports: the decision procedure's verdict is strictly weaker than the proposition it is named for, and the search's bound equation is what closes the gap
evidence.notes: Nat.Hall.criticalB (range 3) nb (singleton 5) reduces to `true`, and 5 is not a member of range 3: Nat.Finset.subsetFixed loops to bound s and answers nothing about indices at or above it (ADR-1644's truncation asymmetry). So the verdict alone does not give the critical branch the inclusion it needs. The proof does not assume it -- Nat.Finset.existsSubset_of_search returns Eq Nat (bound t) (bound s) alongside the verdict, and it is that equation, fed to Nat.Finset.memB_of_subsetFixed_of_bound_le, that upgrades the decision to a pointwise inclusion. The test pins both halves rather than choosing an instance where the predicate happened to answer `false`, which would have hidden the hazard behind a green assertion.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The same test asserts bound (singleton 5) = 6 and bound (range 3) = 3 and that the two are not def-eq, which is why the search cannot return this set and the inductive step never sees it. Without that half the first assertion would read as a defect rather than as a documented boundary.

notes:
epistemic_status and external_status agree: Hall's marriage theorem is from 1935. What is recorded is the position of the flywheel -- the theorem is now a kernel term in this repository with an empty axiom footprint, closing a six-slice sequence that began with necessity in ADR-1608.

Three things the assembly needed that no prior slice's sizing had named, all recorded in ADR-1645: the descent needs an EQUATION and the tree's existing inequality is in the useless direction (F:hall-descent-measure); the search predicate's verdict does not imply inclusion and the search's bound equation is what makes the branch sound; and the exhaustion rule's `false` cannot be reflected into a strict inequality here, because this tree carries `ble_eq_false_of_lt` and not its converse, so the branch decides with lt_or_ge and clashes a rebuilt `true` against the search's `false` instead.

One prior deliverable turned out unusable by the induction it was landed for. Nat.Hall.exists_isMatching_singleton (ADR-1630) is stated at a LITERAL Nat.Finset.singleton a, and an arbitrary s with card s = 1 is not definitionally one; there is no route from the count to the spelling without set extensionality. It is not needed -- the non-critical branch commits one index and recurses on sdiff s (singleton x), which the empty case answers -- so the only base case the induction consumes is exists_isMatching_of_card_le_zero. The singleton lemma remains a correct standalone statement and is recorded as measured-unusable-here rather than dropped.
